source.title: AgentRM: Enhancing Agent Generalization with Reward Modeling
source.authors: Yu Xia; Jing-Ru Fan; Weize Chen; Si-Yu Yan; Xin Cong; Zhong Zhang; Ya-Xi Lu; Yan-Kai Lin; Zhi-Yuan Liu; Mao-Song Sun

page_placements.theme: Weaker or smaller verifiers and reward models improve a stronger generator through test-time selection (reranking, best-of-N)

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some Table 4 values for Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct are flattened and cannot be assigned to individual task columns with confidence.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports a related weak-to-strong transfer in agent tasks: a reward model trained using experience collected by an 8B policy guides inference by other policies, including larger ones. This is a new setting and intervention, not the weak-label fine-tuning method or PGR measure in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The reported cross-policy reward-guided performance results bear on the broader weak-to-strong idea, but the reward model is trained on environment/search-derived rewards and guides test-time search; the stronger policy is not fine-tuned on labels produced by the weaker policy. These results therefore fit no listed claim version. Other comparisons, including policy fine-tuning on expert trajectories and reward-model ablations, do not test the listed weak-to-strong fine-tuning claims.
record.test_reason: AgentRM trains an 8B process reward model on environment-derived MCTS state values, collected with an SFT LLaMA-3-8B policy. It then uses the RM for Best-of-N or beam search over other policies (1B–70B). No strong model is fine-tuned on a weaker model's labels. The comparison is each policy's greedy score against its own RM-guided score, not against a weak supervisor, so no PGR can be computed. The paper calls this "weak-to-strong generalization" (citing Yang et al. 2024), but it is reward-guided test-time search transfer, not the claim's setup. The reader's 'tests'/T3 contradicts its own finding that every version is not_tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that AgentRM, trained on LLaMA-3-8B experience, transfers plug-and-play to other policies with "more pronounced advantages for models with greater scale and potential" (70B +12.6). The ordering is not monotonic in size: the 14B gains 7.2, the 3B 6.8, and the 8B AgentGen 5.9. The improvement is over each policy's own greedy search, not over a weak supervisor.
record.recipe_differences: The reward model is trained on search-tree state values derived from environment outcomes and experience sampled by an 8B policy; it guides Best-of-N inference for other policies. The target policy is not fine-tuned on weak-model labels, and PGR is not measured.
record.method_sensitivity: Reward-guidance gains vary by policy model and task; the 1B policy has several task-level decreases or unchanged scores, while the reported overall score increases.

fits_no_version.finding: An 8B RM trained on states sampled by LLaMA-3-8B raises overall Best-of-5 scores for other policies. Gains over each policy's own greedy baseline are: 70B +12.6, Qwen-14B +7.2, AgentGen +5.9, 3B +6.8, 1B +2.9. Several task-level drops occur (e.g. 1B Sciworld 4.0→0.2; Qwen Toolquery 80.0→48.3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A reward model trained on search experience from a smaller policy can improve test-time search for larger policies. This is reward-guided inference transfer, not weak-label student fine-tuning.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the cited transfer results. The policy is not fine-tuned on labels produced by the weaker model, and the study does not calculate PGR. Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct's task-level cells cannot be reliably assigned from the flattened text.
record.rows_left_out: The task-level Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct results in Table 4 were omitted because the flattened text does not reliably associate the values with task columns. Its overall result is retained as T4-qwen-overall. Other paper results do not bear on the listed weak-label fine-tuning claims.

untested.parts: No strong model is fine-tuned on weak-model labels. There is no weak-supervisor or strong-ceiling comparison and no PGR.
No training change to weak-label fine-tuning is tested.
Gains are reported across policy sizes and tasks, but not PGR or its dependence on supervisor/student size.
No weak-supervision failure mode is tested.

record.verdict_notes: Changed relation from tests/T3 to discusses/T6. The study only uses the phrase weak-to-strong for a different mechanism: a test-time RM trained on environment-grounded values, with no weak labels and no fine-tuning of the strong model. Several AgentGen task rows mix in Qwen2.5-14B cells from the flattened Table 4. AgentGen's true Sciworld/Babyai/Jericho baselines (13.9/39.4/10.8) match Table 1.

versions.untested_parts: The strong policy is not fine-tuned on labels from the weak policy; no weak-supervisor comparison or PGR is reported.
No training change to weak-label fine-tuning or PGR is tested.
The paper compares reward-guided outcomes across policy models and tasks, but does not measure PGR or test how PGR varies with supervisor/student size, task, or representations.
No listed weak-supervision failure mode is tested.
No theoretical conditions for a student beating its supervisor are analyzed.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Section 5.4 and the conclusion describe transfer from 8B-generated experience to stronger policies as weak-to-strong generalization, but measure inference-time search improvements over each policy's greedy baseline.

tranche.reason: Environment-derived state values train the reward model, which guides policy inference. No stronger student is fine-tuned on weaker-model labels, and no listed claim version is tested or used.

source_check.notes: Table 4 explicitly reports gains of 12.6 and 5.9 for 70B and AgentGen; subtracting the displayed rounded endpoints gives 12.5 and 5.8. These are task-performance gains, not PGR.
